## Findings

The tables above are for rewrite prompt v2. Prompt v1 results are quoted where they show what changed. Prompt v2 was written after reading the v1 failures on this same eval set, so its gains here are an optimistic estimate.

1. **Rewrite fixes follow-ups.** Across the 17 follow-up cases, hit@1 goes from 0.53 (naive) to 0.88 and MRR from 0.68 to 0.94; overall hit@3 goes from 0.83 to 1.00. Small talk is detected in 3/3 cases, where naive search returns articles for "Thanks, that's all!".
2. **Pasting the history in is not a substitute.** Config 2 (full history) is no better than naive overall (hit@1 0.60 vs 0.63) and scores 0.00 on corrections, because the superseded topic is still in the query.
3. **BM25 fixes exact codes.** Adding BM25 (config 3 → 4) lifts `exact_code` hit@1 from 0.80 to 1.00 and overall hit@1 from 0.83 to 0.90. Hybrid is the best configuration on every overall metric except hit@3.
4. **Reranking lowers the top-1 result on this set.** Config 5 scores hit@1 0.80 against 0.90 for hybrid alone, and MRR 0.874 against 0.938. The cross-encoder tends to prefer a product page that repeats the product name over the policy article that answers the question. For chat this matters less than it looks: the top five chunks go to Claude together, so their order is not decisive, and the rerank score is what the relevance gate needs (finding 8).
5. **The rewrite prompt mattered more than any retrieval setting.** Prompt v1 added the store name and full product descriptors to its rewrites; v2 tells the rewriter to add only what the question needs. That one change moved config 3 from hit@1 0.70 to 0.83 and config 4 from 0.80 to 0.90, and fixed the v1 error where "the second one" was resolved to the wrong option.
6. **Latency.** Naive search takes under 0.1 s. The rewrite adds about 0.8 s on average (p95 1.7 s). Reranking 10 candidates adds between 0.9 s and 3 s on the laptop used (12th Gen Intel i5-12450H), depending on what else the machine is doing: the full pipeline measured p95 2.6 s in the latest run and 4.7–5.6 s in earlier runs under memory pressure.
7. **Cost.** Each benchmark run after a prompt change makes about 22 Claude calls (one per eval case with history) and 0 on re-runs.

## Chat relevance threshold

`scripts/calibrate_threshold.py` measures the rerank score that the chat's threshold gate sees. Positives are the 30 retrieval cases (score of the best chunk from an expected article); negatives are the 20 questions in `data/eval/negatives.json` (top score), half off-topic and half real support questions that no article covers.

| Threshold | Correct answers kept | Off-topic stopped | Not-covered stopped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | 97% | 100% | 60% |
| **0.05** | **97%** | **100%** | **90%** |
| 0.10 | 97% | 100% | 90% |
| 0.15 | 93% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.30 | 93% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.50 | 87% | 100% | 100% |
| 0.70 | 83% | 100% | 100% |

- Off-topic questions score at most 0.004 and uncovered support questions at most 0.115. The lowest correct answers score 0.002, 0.11, and 0.39.
- **Chosen: 0.05** (`CHAT_MIN_RERANK_SCORE`). It keeps 29 of 30 correct answers and stops every off-topic question. Raising it to 0.15 would stop the last uncovered question but lose a second correct answer; a conventional 0.5 would discard 4 of 30 correct answers.
- The one correct answer lost at any threshold above 0.002 is C-026 ("The zip on my rucksack broke..."): the reranker does not connect "zip" and "rucksack" to "zipper" and "backpack". The chat answers it with "I don't have that information".
- Uncovered questions that pass the gate are still caught by Claude, which returns `not_found` when the chunks do not contain the answer.
- Scoring each chunk against both the rewritten query and the original question (taking the higher score) was measured and changed nothing at this threshold, so it was not adopted: it would double the rerank time.
- With prompt v1 rewrites a cut-off of even 0.01 removed correct answers. The search endpoint therefore still applies no cut-off by default (`RERANK_MIN_SCORE=0`); only the chat gate uses one.

## Chat end-to-end results

All 53 messages (33 eval conversations and 20 negatives) sent to `POST /chat` on the real models and Claude, with `scripts/evaluate_chat.py`. A reply counts as correct when its kind is the expected one and, for answers, a cited source is an expected article.

| Group | Messages | Correct | Grounding failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| Follow-ups (pronoun, ellipsis, correction, multi-reference) | 17 | 17 | 0 |
| Exact code | 5 | 5 | 0 |
| Paraphrase | 4 | 3 | 0 |
| Already standalone | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| Small talk | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Off-topic | 10 | 10 | 0 |
| Not covered | 10 | 10 | 0 |
| **Total** | **53** | **52** | **0** |

- The one miss is C-026, stopped by the threshold gate as described above.
- 29 answers were written, with 2.2 citations each on average. No answer needed the grounding correction attempt, and the output guardrail masked nothing.
- Median latency was 4.2 s and the maximum 6.5 s per message. The run made 50 Claude calls: one per message that reached the answer step, with rewrites served from cache.
- What this does not measure: "correct" checks the kind of reply and the source article, not every sentence. A sample of answers was read by hand and matched their sources. The grounding check verifies quotes and numbers; a sentence with no number and no citation is not verified.

## Acceptance criteria (workflow doc 9.5)

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| All article endpoints work; a new article is immediately findable by vector and keyword search | Met (integration tests) |
| Full pipeline (5) beats naive (1) on hit@1, hit@3, and MRR | Met: 0.80 / 0.93 / 0.874 vs 0.63 / 0.83 / 0.767 |
| `exact_code`: hybrid (4) beats vector-only (3) | Met: hit@1 1.00 vs 0.80 |
| Follow-up patterns: rewrite (3) beats naive (1) | Met: hit@1 0.88 vs 0.53, MRR 0.94 vs 0.68 |
| Rerank (5) improves hit@1 or MRR over config 4 | **Not met**: hit@1 0.80 vs 0.90, MRR 0.874 vs 0.938 (finding 4) |
| Full pipeline p95 latency < 3 s on CPU | Met in the latest run (2.6 s); **not met** in earlier runs under memory pressure (4.7–5.6 s). Chat adds the answer call on top: median 4.2 s per message |
| Total real Anthropic calls ≤ 50 for the whole build | Met for the original build (39). The cap was later raised to 500 by the owner for the chat feature; 126 used so far |
| All quality gates green | Met |

## What was not done, and why

- **Dropping the reranker from search.** On this set hybrid alone ranks better (finding 4). The reranker was kept because the chat gate depends on its score, and because 30 cases are too few to remove a stage on.
- **Synonym handling for the reranker.** C-026 needs "zip/rucksack" matched to "zipper/backpack". A larger reranker or query expansion would address it; neither was tried.
- **A harmful-content classifier.** The output guardrail is pattern matching for contact details, card-like numbers, and links. Nothing judges tone or harmful content; the grounding check is what keeps answers to the help content.
- **Temperature 0.** The model family used rejects a non-default temperature. Consistency comes from typed output, the grounding check, and the answer cache.
- **Sample size.** 30 retrieval cases and 20 negatives: one case is 0.03 of hit@1, and the threshold was chosen on the same data it is reported on.
